claims.claim: The proposal requests 420,000 ADA plus a 105,000 ADA contingency reserve for a part-time Oura maintainer over 12 months at an annual rate of $105,000 USD.
The total requested withdrawal is 540,750 ADA, consisting of 525,000 ADA for Oura Maintenance and Enhancement and a 15,750 ADA Intersect Budget Administration fee.
Oura is a Rust-native pipeline tool that connects to Cardano nodes, monitors blockchain events, and routes matching patterns to pluggable outputs for processing.
Oura supports multiple data sources including N2C, N2N, S3, Mithril, and UTxO RPC, and supports sinks including Kafka, Elasticsearch, AWS services, RabbitMQ, Redis, SQL databases, and webhooks.
The proposal states that Oura has 654 commits, 288 stars, 79 forks, and 58 contributors, and links to the Oura GitHub repository.
The proposal states that Oura is used across the ecosystem for indexing, monitoring, analytics, and real-time event processing.
The proposal states that it achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase.
The proposal states that the requested amount does not breach the applicable 350M Net Change Limit for Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at the time of submission.
The proposal states that independent oversight will be provided through Intersect and technically capable third parties with reporting obligations and milestone-based disbursement controls.
The proposal states that TxPipe has received funding through 30 Project Catalyst proposals across Funds 9 through 14, with 26 delivered and 4 under development and on schedule.

summary: The document requests 540,750 ADA for 12 months of Oura maintenance, describes technical scope and governance routing, and provides several checkable references, but much of the value, adoption, budget reasonableness, and delivery history is asserted rather than fully evidenced in the anchor text.
